San Francisco de Yuruani is located in the Gran Sabana of southeastern Venezuela. Open savanna and distant mountains define the settlement's natural surroundings. On routes to Roraima, it serves as a stopping point before the trekking portion of the journey.

Staying here allows travelers to shift from a long drive to preparations for the mountain route. The onward journey to the trailhead connects the settlement with smaller communities of the Gran Sabana. Its role in the trip is particularly clear in combination with a multiday ascent to the plateau.

San Francisco is a church and monastery complex in Lima's historic center. It is one of the notable monuments of colonial architecture in the Peruvian capital: its facades and interiors combine Baroque and Neoclassical elements.

The complex is known for its monastery courtyards, religious paintings and sculptures, library and historical archive. The library collection preserves old theological books and other publications. Together, these spaces reveal the monastery as a cultural monument rather than simply a church.

Beneath the complex are catacombs that were used for burials during the colonial period. They can be visited as part of certain tours, but their presence does not mean they are included in every sightseeing excursion in Lima. Before visiting, it is important to distinguish between viewing the complex, entering its interior rooms and making a separate descent into the catacombs.

The San Francisco monastic complex in Tlaxcala offers a glimpse into the first decades of the region's Christian history. Rather than lavish Baroque facades, its appeal lies in its early architecture, open spaces and peaceful monastery courtyard.

The former monastery church became the Cathedral of the Assumption; the complex is also associated with the Regional Museum of Tlaxcala. In 2021, the ensemble was included in the UNESCO World Heritage property dedicated to early monasteries on the slopes of Popocatépetl. A walk around the grounds complements a visit to the city's historic center.

## Theatres, museums and colonial buildings: what to see in San José

San José is Costa Rica's capital and also its largest city. It lies in the very center of the country, which is why almost all tourist routes begin here. Historic buildings sit naturally alongside modern glass-and-concrete structures, giving San José its distinctive appearance.

San José became the capital of Costa Rica in 1837, although it had been founded 100 years earlier. Several architectural styles have shaped the city. Most buildings are colonial or Neoclassical in style and no more than 5 stories high. There are modern high-rises too, concentrated in the city's central and business districts. The outskirts have many villas and private houses surrounded by greenery. The National Theatre building is considered the most beautiful theatre building in Latin America. Numerous museums house rich collections on a wide variety of subjects. The city has first-class hotels, the National Stadium, a zoo, shops, cinemas and restaurants.

## The many sides of San José

Both in the city and nearby, visitors will find plenty to explore: the majestic cathedral, the Simón Bolívar Zoo, museums devoted to gold and jade, and even a university museum of exotic insects. Small markets and streets have a special atmosphere, while coffee plantations, butterfly farms and even volcanoes await travelers in the surrounding area. Every year around December 15 — more precisely, on the Saturday closest to December 15 — San José hosts an evening carnival called the Festival of Light.

## San Juan del Sur — everything for a relaxing vacation!

A very welcoming town filled with the charm of complete tranquility. Beautiful landscapes open up from the tops of the hills surrounding the town. The scenic beaches of this stretch of Pacific coast attract surfers from all over the world, as well as fishing enthusiasts. And, of course, there is the remarkable underwater world, with its diversity of species and underwater sights.
